title: The Medical Malacology Collection (Fiocruz/CMM, Brazil): importance of an institutionalized and accredited biological reference collection
content:
Abstract
The Medical Malacology Collection (Fiocruz/CMM, Brazil) houses specimens of freshwater molluscs, with emphasis on the genus Biomphalaria, an intermediate host of Schistosoma mansoni. Since its creation in 1993, the Fiocruz/CMM has supported research, teaching, and public health through the collection, preservation, identification, and provision of specimens and metadata. Institutionalized within Fiocruz and accredited by the National Institute of Metrology, Quality, and Technology (ISO/IEC 17025) for the morphological and molecular identification of Biomphalaria, the Fiocruz/CMM has consolidated itself as a reference collection for medically important molluscs in Brazil, contributing to the standardization and reliability of technical procedures. The collection is accessible through a digital platform and has been used in taxonomic, genetic, and ecological studies, in addition to training activities and collaborations with health institutions. This article describes the main aspects of curation, services offered, types of materials preserved, and scientific contributions generated by the Fiocruz/CMM. It also highlights the role of the collection as a source of information on mollusc biodiversity of medical importance and as a complementary tool for schistosomiasis surveillance and control strategies.
